explanation: No coherent trigger: fires on a wide assortment of tokens (CJK characters like 語/版/見/質, function words such as 'its', 'of', 'that', idiom completions like 'passed away', 'in accordance', 'broad sense', code identifiers, digits, word fragments). Weak and mid-range examples are similarly scattered nouns and function words; no single token class or context predicts strong firing.

Mixed: strong on '+' / '=' in generated math expressions ('-v**3 + v**2', 'Let f = u - g'), on 'You will' at the start of instructional text, on 'to' after 'closest/relative/born ... ,', and on assorted other tokens (bold, first, review, :each, de, output). No single shared context explains the set.

Fires in encyclopedic/Wikipedia-style stub text at the token that begins a standard formula continuation: 'described' in 'Moths/Beetles described in' or 'It was described by', the space before a year in 'is a 1960 film/2006...', 'in' in 'a moth in the family'. Weaker offshoots fire on predictable verb/preposition continuations in formal prose ('meet criteria', 'resistance to', 'protected by').

Diffuse: the single max is a digit in an arithmetic answer; the rest (all <=55%) are scattered over name fragments in Korean/ancient names, 'its' in 'and/or its affiliates', commas, code identifier pieces, and miscellaneous tokens. No clear common feature.

Mainly fires on 'Software' in the GPL license boilerplate phrase 'the Free Software Foundation' (moderate-strong, ~60-70%); other strong hits are second pieces of multi-token proper names or technical terms (es-ri, R-aman, Rod-ham, Plan-ck, potent-iation, run-at). Strongest single hit is a newline in a legal opinion footnote.

Fires on tokens in generic/boilerplate web and expository prose where a predictable continuation follows, e.g. 'you' in 'By using this website you agree/consent' cookie notices, 'include' after 'Such desirable traits', 'that' in 'news that matter', commas and periods in marketing/instruction text, plus scattered code tokens. Broad and not tightly defined.

Fires on the ';

' (or '

') that ends a Java/Kotlin/Go 'package ...' or PHP 'namespace ...' declaration at the top of a source file, right before the imports/uses. Weaker on similar file-header boundaries like the end of a license comment '*/

' before code, '#include' or 'using' after a license header.

Mixed: strongest on the space before a numeric coefficient in generated polynomials ('s**3 - 8*s**2', 'z**2 + 1'), on '(p' / 'SD ' before statistics values, and on a variety of ordinary verb/function-word tokens in prose ('play by the rules', 'ability to perform', 'crank out'). No single consistent trigger.

Fires on tokens inside parenthesized abbreviations/acronyms introduced right after a spelled-out term, e.g. 'end stage renal failure (ES[RD])', '(C[JR])', '(DRAM)', '(AMI)', typically the second token of the acronym; also on name fragments inside parentheses or after an initial ('M[uld]row', 'D[ipt]era'). Plain words not in an abbreviation context barely fire.

Fires near the start of a document or section, especially the first token of the opening sentence of a Wikipedia-style article right after the title line ('In the theory', 'Šeduva () is', 'P'ano, 'G'oddess, 'K'altbrunn) and the first word of a new problem ('What is'). Other hits are scattered mid-sentence tokens with weaker activation.

Fires mostly on byte-fragment tokens of emojis and multi-byte characters (mojibake '�', 😂, 😉, broken CJK/Cyrillic bytes, box-drawing '══'), with weaker scattered activations on mid-word subword pieces of unusual words (fol, ats, ith, ash, ap) and code tokens like '(define'.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that begins with an 'n'/capital after a hyphen or space and continues as a multi-token rare word, especially chemistry names ('-n'itro, '-N'ormetaz, ' n'ifedipine, ' nucle'otides) and other proper-name/word starts that get split (N'ippur, D'ibr'ugarh, Pen'ob'scot, ' l'izards). Common whole words do not fire.

Fires on a mid-word subword piece (usually the stem right after a prefix or first fragment) of words split into several tokens, most strongly in Russian text (с-мотр-ели, вид-но, сохран-ить, объ-ясн-ить) and similar in English/Latin-derived words (Infer-ior, infer-otemporal, iod-ine, refer, interfer-es, ADVERT-ising).

Mixed: fires on assorted tokens in code (Aliyun SDK identifiers, XML/HTML tags, CSS ':', quotes), CJK characters in Chinese/Japanese text, digits in ISBNs/postal codes/dates, and function words in license boilerplate ('or (at your option)'). Possibly a loose 'East-Asian/technical context' feature but too heterogeneous to state one rule.
